summary: Nearly all visitors need a Ugandan visa, applied for online through the official eVisa portal (USD 50 single entry) before travel; East African Community citizens move freely, and a list of mostly African, Caribbean and Commonwealth countries is visa-exempt.

vaccinations.text: Malaria is present year-round throughout Uganda, including Kampala. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of Uganda, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

The UK Foreign Office says electronic cigarettes and shisha are illegal, and that buying or trading parts of protected wild animals without a licence can lead to prosecution, a prison sentence or a fine.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are accepted only by major hotels, airlines and some car rental agencies, and that there are foreign exchange bureaus at most border crossings and in major cities.

safety.text: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Uganda, including in places visited by tourists and in national parks; take particular care in western Uganda near the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Criminals may target tourists who show signs of wealth. Same-sex sexual activity is illegal, and the Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 sets long prison sentences and, in some cases, the death penalty.

tips.text: Uganda dropped its yellow fever certificate requirement for entry on 2 October 2026. Vaccination is still recommended because the disease occurs here, and a later destination may ask for the certificate if you arrive from Uganda.
Combining Uganda with Kenya and Rwanda? The USD 100 East Africa Tourist Visa covers all three countries for 90 days with multiple entries between them. Apply through the country you enter first.
Uganda has no visa on arrival for most nationalities. Apply at visas.immigration.go.ug before flying and travel with the printed approval letter; avoid unofficial visa websites.

Gorilla-tracking permits in Bwindi and Mgahinga cost USD 800 for foreign non-residents (USD 600 in the low-season months of April, May and November). Foreign non-residents can book them only through a licensed tour operator, and the Uganda Wildlife Authority now issues permits only on full payment.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Uganda?
faq.answer: Most visitors do — Uganda uses an eVisa system, with the single-entry tourist visa at USD 50 applied for online before travel. East African Community citizens enter freely, and nationals of a list of mostly African, Caribbean and Commonwealth countries are visa-exempt.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Uganda?
faq.answer: Uganda has moved visa issuance online. You should apply at visas.immigration.go.ug before travel and carry the approval letter, which is exchanged for the visa on arrival. Airlines generally will not board visa-required passengers without the approval.

faq.question: What is the East Africa Tourist Visa?
faq.answer: A joint USD 100 visa covering Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda for 90 days, with multiple entries between the three countries. Apply through the country you enter first — if that is Uganda, via the official Ugandan eVisa portal.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Uganda?
faq.answer: No longer. Uganda's immigration service announced on 2 October 2026 that a yellow fever certificate is not required for entry. Vaccination is still recommended, and the East African Tourist Visa and multiple-entry visa applications still list the certificate as a document to upload.

faq.question: How long does the Uganda eVisa take?
faq.answer: Uganda's immigration service does not publish a processing time, so apply well before you travel. You will need a passport scan, photo and travel details.
